points.description: States that the bandwidth-delay product equals the link capacity (bandwidth) multiplied by the one-way propagation delay, e.g. 10 Mbps × 20 ms, or equivalently BDP = C × Tprop. Do not accept use of round-trip time or a statement naming only one factor.
points.partial_credit: Half mark if the answer mentions both link capacity/bandwidth and propagation delay but does not state that they are multiplied, or gives an incorrect operation.

levels.says: Mentions both link capacity/bandwidth and propagation delay but does not state that they are multiplied, or gives an incorrect operation.

points.description: Explains that the bandwidth-delay product is the amount of data that can be in flight / in transit / on the link at one time. Accept equivalent wording such as the link's capacity to hold data in the pipe. Do not accept merely restating the formula or saying it is the total data sent.
points.partial_credit: Half mark if the answer says data is in transit/on the link but does not make clear that it is the amount/capacity of data that can be in flight.

levels.says: Says data is in transit/on the link but does not make clear that it is the amount/capacity of data that can be in flight.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the formula (capacity multiplied by one-way propagation delay) and the meaning (amount of data that can be in flight on the link). Half marks are available for a partially correct formula or a partially correct meaning. No marks are earned for an answer that gives neither the formula nor the meaning.
